Radials Folder
Finding Plasticity's radials folder…
Plasticity loads every radial menu in .plasticity/radials when it starts. Turning one off moves its file to a radials-disabled folder next to it, where Plasticity doesn't look; turning it on moves it back. Restart Plasticity to see changes.
A disabled menu can be deleted, which moves its file to the Recycle Bin (Trash on a Mac).
Each menu is checked against your keyboard shortcuts and your other menus: you're told which shortcut or menu opens it, and warned when one you turn off is still used, when a menu opens one that isn't there, or when two menus share the same command name (Plasticity can only open one of them).
Open in Create loads a menu into the builder so you can change it.

Theme File
No file open
To use a theme by hand, save it as theme.json in your .plasticity/config/v2 folder and restart Plasticity. Colours you pick in Plasticity's Preferences > Appearance override the file.
Plasticity Theme
Finding Plasticity's theme folder…
Apply sends this theme straight to Plasticity, and Reset puts Plasticity's own colours back. Restart Plasticity afterwards to see the change. Plasticity also has its own Reset to defaults button at the bottom of Preferences > Appearance.
Starter Themes
Save the colours you have now under your own name. They appear at the top of the list, under My Themes.
Only the colours we've seen Plasticity use are shown. Turn on Advanced to see the rest too, in case a future version uses them or we've missed one.
Neutral
Accent
Supporting
A hollow dot means we haven't seen that shade used in Plasticity.
Viewport
These need Plasticity 26.2 or later, and match the colour settings in Plasticity's Preferences > Appearance. Clear a box to go back to Plasticity's default. Supporting colour saves Supporting as a single colour, the same way Plasticity does. It colours the reticle (the dot under the cursor) and the Scene folder icon.
A few colours are built into Plasticity and no theme can change them: the yellow selection outline, blue curves and the faint lines between control points. Plasticity also draws the grid a little darker than the colour you pick, and the preview does the same. Settings that showed no effect (the old edge values, edge sizes, matcap tint, dialog and white) stay in the file; turn on Advanced to see and change them.
Everything Else in the File
Colours and sizes in the theme file that we haven't seen Plasticity use, including the spare colour ranges Plasticity's own theme files carry. They're here in case a future version uses them, or in case we've missed one.
Drop PNG, JPG, WebP or EXR matcaps here
from your files or straight from a browser, or click to choose files
To Add
Installed
Matcaps Folder
Finding Plasticity's matcaps folder…
Collections
A collection is a set of matcaps to have switched on, such as one for surfacing and a calmer one for solid modelling. Enable the matcaps you want, then click Save Enabled as New. Use Collection enables its matcaps and disables the rest, which move to matcaps-disabled; nothing is deleted. Update saves what's enabled now into the chosen collection.
Files We Make
Plasticity wants each matcap as a pair with the same name: an EXR for the texture and a PNG for the picker. Files you add are copied as they are under the clean name (spaces become _). Only the missing half of the pair is made, at the sizes above.
A JPG or WebP has no transparency, so the files made from it are cut to a circle.
Tinted (beta) saves NAME.json containing { isTinted: true }, which lets Plasticity tint the matcap with the material colour. Plasticity multiplies the matcap by the material colour, so tinting can only darken and shift colours. It works best on neutral matcaps with low saturation (greys, silvers, clay); colourful matcaps don't tint well. A tinted matcap shows a row of examples (red, yellow, green, blue and grey materials) next to its checkbox.
Disable moves a matcap into a matcaps-disabled folder next to this one, where Plasticity doesn't look. Enable moves it back. A disabled matcap can be deleted, which moves its files to the Recycle Bin (Trash on a Mac).
Reorder… lets you drag matcaps into order, then renames them 01_Name, 02_Name and so on so they sort that way. Remove Numbers takes the numbers off again. Restart Plasticity to see changes.
Installed matcaps are only changed when you click: Fix, Tinted, Disable, Enable, Delete or Apply Order.
Drop EXR or HDR environments here
2:1 panoramas, from your files or straight from a browser, or click to choose files
To Add
Installed
Environments Folder
Finding Plasticity's environments folder…
Collections
A collection is a set of environments to have switched on, such as a few studio lights for product shots. Enable the ones you want, then click Save Enabled as New. Use Collection enables its environments and disables the rest, which move to environments-disabled; nothing is deleted.
Files We Make
Plasticity wants each environment as a pair with the same name: an EXR for the lighting and a PNG thumbnail for the picker. Both are 2:1 panoramas (equirectangular).
An EXR you add is shrunk to the size above if it's bigger, and otherwise copied as it is, under the clean name (spaces become _). Choose Keep the original size to copy every EXR as it is. A small PNG thumbnail is made from it. The most this can read is 8K (8192 × 4096).
An HDR (.hdr or .hdri) is converted: it's made into a 16-bit EXR at the size above, plus the thumbnail. The HDR itself isn't copied.
Disable moves an environment into an environments-disabled folder next to this one, where Plasticity doesn't look. Enable moves it back. A disabled environment can be deleted, which moves its files to the Recycle Bin (Trash on a Mac).
Reorder… renames them 01_Name, 02_Name and so on so they sort that way. Restart Plasticity to see changes.
Installed environments are only changed when you click: Fix, Disable, Enable, Delete or Apply Order.
Drop TTF or OTF fonts here
they're converted for Plasticity's Text command, or click to choose files
To Install
Installed
Fonts Folder
Finding Plasticity's fonts folder…
Plasticity's Text command can use your own fonts. When it starts, it loads every .typeface-json file in .plasticity/fonts, the same format as its built-in fonts. This tab converts TTF and OTF fonts into that format and puts them there.
Restart Plasticity after installing or removing fonts: it only reads them when it starts. Save your work before closing it.
Each style is its own font: add Regular and Bold files separately if you want both. A font can only show the characters it contains. Ligatures and the extra styles inside variable fonts aren't carried over.
Very decorative or overlapping letters can make awkward geometry for extrudes and fillets, even when the font converts cleanly. Simple, solid typefaces work best.
Check that your font's licence lets you use it this way. Fonts whose own settings say they mustn't be embedded are flagged before you install them.
This tab uses Plasticity's fonts folder, which works in Plasticity 26.1.3 but isn't an official feature, so a future version could change it.
Plasticity is open. It saves its own list of packs, which could undo changes made here, so close it before turning packs on or off.
Asset Packs
Pack Folders
Add the folders where you keep .plasticitypack files, on any drive. Their subfolders are searched too.
Collections
A collection is a set of packs to have on, such as your sci-fi kits or your hardware packs. Turn on the packs you want, then click Save On Packs as New. Use Collection turns its packs on and the rest off; the pack files themselves never move. Update saves the packs on now into the chosen collection.
Plasticity's Pack List
Finding asset-packs.json…
A pack is on when it's in Plasticity's list of asset packs (asset-packs.json), which is what the Assets panel shows. Turning one off only takes it out of that list; the pack file stays where it is.
Close Plasticity before making changes, then open it to see them: it reads the list when it starts and saves it again itself. Each change keeps the previous list as asset-packs.json.bak, and Restore Backup puts it back. The list you had before this app first changed it stays in asset-packs.json.original.
Packs you opened in Plasticity from somewhere else are listed at the bottom, with any whose file has been moved or deleted.

Add a Shortcut
Keymap File
Finding Plasticity's keymap.json…
Plasticity keeps your shortcuts in keymap.json. Only the ones you add or change are stored there; the rest are Plasticity's built-in shortcuts, listed here from Plasticity 26.1.3.
To open one of your radial menus with a shortcut, choose it from the radial menu list under Command. It lists the menus in Plasticity's radials folder and the folder the Radial Menus tab saves to; Browse… picks any other radial file. Plasticity only loads menus from its radials folder, so save or copy a menu there for its shortcut to work.
Click the Keys box and press the keys. Mouse buttons work too: click the box, then press the middle or a side button. Tab and Escape can't be recorded, so type them instead (tab, escape).
Where sets when a shortcut works. Everywhere covers the whole window while no command is running. Plasticity's own viewport keys, and the keys inside commands (like X for the X axis while moving), still take priority in their own places.
Turn Off stops a built-in shortcut (it's saved as unset!). Reset and Remove take your shortcut out, so Plasticity's own comes back.
Nothing changes until you click Save to Plasticity. The file you had is kept as keymap.json.bak, and Restore Backup brings it back. The one from before this app first changed it stays in keymap.json.original. Restart Plasticity if new shortcuts don't work straight away.
Plasticity is open. It reads these files when it starts and saves some of them again itself, so close it before switching profiles.
Profiles
New Profile
In Plasticity Now
Reading your Plasticity folders…
Tray
Build a profile out of the things you have made: one of My Themes (or a starter), and a matcap, environment and asset pack collection. Make the collections in their own tabs first. Leave as it is keeps that part out of the profile, so switching never touches it.
A profile follows its theme and collections by name, so changing a collection changes every profile that uses it. A copy is kept with the profile too, and used if the theme or collection is deleted. The ones on now saves a fixed list instead.
Use switches Plasticity to the profile. theme.json and asset-packs.json are replaced, with the old one kept as .bak. Matcaps, environments and radial menus that aren't in the profile are turned off (moved to their -disabled folders), and the profile's are turned on. Nothing is deleted, and Undo Last Switch puts back the setup from before.
Close Plasticity before switching, then open it again to see the change. Keyboard shortcuts and fonts aren't part of profiles.
